title: Loop back: deciding based on words
idea: LOOP. No new concept. Review string comparison in decisions, case sensitivity, and matching one of several words.

exercises.explanation: color equals 'red', so 'Stop'. (Review of string comparison.)

exercises.prompt: String comparison with == treats 'Red' and 'red' as the same.
exercises.explanation: == is case-sensitive, so 'Red' and 'red' differ. (Review of case sensitivity.)
'Sun' matches the second side of 'or', so 'Weekend'. (Review of or with strings.)
== compares the strings. (Review of == for words.)
'MAYBE' is not 'yes', so the else runs. (Review of string == + else.)

exercises.prompt: To accept 'north', 'south', 'east', or 'west' as a valid direction, you would use...
exercises.explanation: Any one of several words -> 'or'. (Review of or for multiple matches.)
size is 'M', matching the elif: 'Medium'. (Review of elif with strings.)

exercises.prompt: An else branch is a good way to handle any word you did not explicitly list.
exercises.explanation: else catches unexpected words, like an invalid size. (Review of else as catch-all.)

exercises.prompt: A quiz checks 'if answer == "Paris"' and the user typed 'paris'. Why is it marked wrong?
exercises.explanation: The capital P matters in ==. Plan for case if needed. (Review of case sensitivity.)
'apple' matches the elif, so 'Red'. (Review of elif ladder with strings.)
